title: Fifa plans Israel v Palestine fixture as opening game of new under-15s tournament - The Guardian
content: Tournament open to all Fifa members, including Russia Fifa wants to schedule a symbolic match between Israel and Palestine as the opening game of a new under-15s tournament in the US in September. Although not an official under‑15 World Cup, the competition will be open to all 211 Fifa members, including Russia, whose national team remain banned at senior level. Fifa announced details of the tournament last December and has grand plans for the opening game because Gianni Infantino remains determined to use football as a vehicle to promote peace and global unity. Infantino experienced embarrassment in April when an attempt to orchestrate a handshake between the Palestinian and Israeli delegates at the governing body’s congress in Vancouver backfired. The Palestinian Football Association president, Jibril Rajoub, refused to stand alongside the Israel FA’s vice‑president, Basim Sheikh Suliman, in an awkward moment towards the end of the 76th Fifa congress despite repeated entreaties from Infantino. This experience does not appear to have deterred Fifa’s president from attempting to play peacemaker, however, with a proposal under active consideration to open the under-15s tournament with a game between Israel and Palestine. The venue for the tournament has not been confirmed but Miami is regarded as the most likely. Fifa has extensive offices in the city. The first tournament will be a boys’ competition, with a girls’ edition to be staged 12 months later, before Fifa moves to organise two separate festivals each year from 2028. Fifa sources rejected the suggestion that attempting to meddle in Israeli‑Palestinian politics was dangerous given events in Vancouver. Infantino is understood to be central to the initiative and made reference to the under-15s tournament after Rajoub declined to shake Suliman’s hand. “Let me thank the two representatives from Israel and from Palestine, who have the same rights, duties and obligations, who are members of Fifa,” Infantino said. “We will work together, let’s work together to give hope to the children, let’s work together for that. “We have a beautiful under‑15 tournament coming up, where we will invite all 211 countries to participate, all the children of the world, let’s do it for that. Let’s work together. You have my commitment, you have the support of the whole room.” One Fifa source said a handshake in Vancouver had been agreed in advance, only for Rajoub to change his mind during the speeches. The Palestinian delegates were unrepentant in the immediate aftermath with their FA’s vice-president, Susan Shalabi, telling Reuters: “I cannot shake the hand of someone the Israelis have brought to whitewash their fascism and genocide. We are suffering.”

title: 2027 Mercedes-AMG GLE63 S and GLS63 Adopt the Flat-Plane Crank V-8 - Road & Track
content: While the updated interior balances big screens with physical controls. Mercedes-Benz launched its revised GLE-Class and GLS-Class SUVs earlier this year, and now it’s AMG’s turn to get in on the fun. On Monday, Mercedes pulled the covers off the 2027 AMG GLE63 S and GLS63. The big news here is the engine under the hood of these two performance SUVs. Mercedes says they’re both fitted with a new AMG version of the M177 Evo engine—the 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 with the new flat-plane crankshaft. We’ve seen this new engine in non-AMG models already. where it makes 530 horsepower and 553 pound-feet of torque. AMG turns up the heat and raises those figures to 603 horsepower and 627 pound-feet of torque for both of these new models. Mercedes is being coy on the details for now, but says this engine has “an optimized injection system, newly designed intake and exhaust ports, a revised intake camshaft, as well as improvements to the compressor wheel and turbocharger housing.” It also has a new generation integrated starter generator for the 48-volt mild-hybrid system that supplies power at lower engine speeds. Mercedes claims the assist is worth 23 horsepower and 151 pound-feet of torque. The power figures are identical to what these SUVs offered before. However, acceleration times are improved. The GLE63 S chops one tenth off its time for a 0-60 mile-per-hour sprint in 3.6 seconds, while the GLS63 chops two tenths, making its 0-60 only 3.9 seconds. Top speed is the same for both at 174 mph. Just like the M177 Evo in the non-AMG models, this flat-plane crank V-8 doesn’t scream to a super-high redline. In fact, its peak horsepower is actually made in a slightly lower rpm range than the previous cross-plane crank version of this engine. Peak torque is identical, coming on as low as 2500 rpm. Mercedes developed the M177 Evo to offer a high-performance V-8 engine that meets ever-tougher emissions regulations; to that end, it has a new AMG Performance exhaust system fitted with a particulate filter worldwide, but AMG still promises a “highly dynamic expression” when in the Sport+ drive mode. “Our V-8 is a central component of our performance DNA and the ideal heart for the new GLE63 S and GLS63,” says AMG boss Michael Schiebe. “For years, the V-8 has stood for impressive performance and great popularity among our customers. With the new generation M177 Evo, we have fundamentally revised the power unit and secured its presence in our portfolio for the long term. The result is an engine that impresses with agile response, strong performance and a pronounced appetite for revs—while at the same time meeting increasingly demanding regulations worldwide.” Outside the powertrain, the biggest difference you’ll notice in these updated AMG models is the design. The front ends are redesigned with the new framed AMG radiator grille, larger air intakes and LED headlights with the three-pointed star logo used as the DRL design. The same pattern is repeated for the taillights, and per usual with V-8-powered AMG models, a distinctive quad exhaust sits integrated into the rear fascia. The freshened interior mirrors what you see on the non-AMG models. Of greatest interest for us is a new AMG steering wheel that now features a physical toggle for cruise control and scroll wheel for volume, replacing the touch controls used previously. The only photo Mercedes provided shows a swath of carbon fiber trim in the GLS63, and the latest MB.OS infotainment system sprawled across the three large interior screens. Most of the underpinnings and performance features are similar to what AMG offered in the past. It has AMG’s Ride Control+ that consists of air suspension and adaptive dampers; it also has Active Ride Control, bringing active roll stabilization that uses active electromechanical stabilizers on both axles to reduce roll. AMG says the ESP system (stability control) is newly developed for this refresh, and offers “even more precise control strategies.” Another nice update for folks who would like to custom-order their example is an expansion of Mercedes’s Manufaktur program for the GLE and GLS. The GLE63 S pictured here is in the newly available Ireland Mid Green Metallic, while the GLS63 is finished in the also-new Mystic Blue Metallic. These new GLE and GLS AMG models will arrive in dealerships this fall, with pricing to come closer to launch. We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we back.

title: Gordon V. Poad - Channel 3000
content: Beginning of dialog window. Escape will cancel and close the window. Live updates all day, breaking news as it happens and weather every 10 minutes Gordon V. Poad, age 86, of Lone Rock passed away June 8, 2026 surrounded by family. He was born August 28, 1939 the son of Gordon and Bernadine (McCarville) Poad. He was united in marriage to Joan Hackl on April 20, 1959. 67 years of marriage and three super, good children. He always boasted and was very proud of those 2 facts. He was a longtime member of the Lone Rock Community Congregational Church. Gordon’s passion was heavy equipment, farming and big trucks. He was able to accomplish all these things in his lifetime. After working for Icke Construction and Bob Ewers Excavating, he started his own construction business. During this time, raising beef cattle on the farm. This is when the show steer era started. Taking it a step farther by cash cropping and custom combining. This in turn led to needing a truck to haul the grain. P&P Grain, Inc. was established. Not one, but a fleet. Mission accomplished. Hobbies were numerous. Deer, bobcat, coyote hunting and trapping on the back forty. Elk in Colorado, bear in Canada and Northern, WI, and exotic deer in Texas. He managed to have a Cabela’s in his own home. His love of horses took him to South Dakota, riding in the Badlands with his cowboy friends. Retirement years brought coffee clutches and breakfasts most mornings. No gossip shared, as men don’t gossip, so he said. Much advice was given to his children and grandkids producing many eye rolls. He is survived by his wife, Joan; children, Gordy (Sherry) Poad, Kim (Dale) Ewers, Randy (Jen) Poad; grandchildren, Holly, Jenna, and Lacey Poad, Dale and Samantha Ewers, Paige (Mills) Meier and Libbi Poad; 6 great-grandchildren, other relatives and friends. He was preceded in death by his parents, sisters, Julie (Frank) Bruhn and Lottie (Bob) Schreurs; and lifelong friend since childhood, Milo Mercer. A Memorial service will be held on Saturday, June 13, 2026 at 11:30 A.M. at the Lone Rock Community Congregational Church. Visitation will be held on Saturday at the Church from 9:00 A.M. until the time of the service. In lieu of flowers memorials may be made to Walk with G.R.A.C.E. or the Lone Rock EMS. Sometime last year, a photo of Christy Turlington doing yoga came across my desk. How alarmingly chic this neckline looked on her, I thought. The rotund V elegantly framing her chest was a far cry from the 2010s deep V and its reputation as the uniform of obnoxious hipsters and greasy guys who hang out at the Jersey Shore. I’ve been longing for the right V-neck T-shirt since then, disappointed when I reach into my closet and find only crewnecks. It’s been more than a decade since I’ve regularly worn the V style — back in the day, usually paired with skinny jeans, a lethal side part, and a Charming Charlie bubble necklace in a sickly shade of coral — and I was finally ready to release my prior associations with the silhouette and seek more modern pastures. I was craving something fresh to fill the V-shaped hole in my closet. My criteria as I searched for the perfect V-neck T-shirt: I wanted it unfussy but able to be dressed up; not so cropped that it exposed several inches of midriff, but not so long that it bunched awkwardly at my hips; and ideally made using natural fibers rather than synthetic. Though it wasn’t crucial, it would be a bonus if the V were rounded like Turlington’s. In other words, I wanted a V-neck that felt closer to CBK than “Party Rock Anthem,” and I tested eight options between $10 and $115 to find the perfect one. For reference, I’m five-foot-eight and typically wear an extra-small in T-shirts, but I sized up and down a few times as noted below. New! You can now save this product for later. The V is high, slightly rounded, and not too in your face. You can easily dress this tee up. New! You can now save this product for later. I went one size up and loved the fit. It's the ideal length and has the softest fabric of the bunch. New! You can now save this product for later. A more casual V, and the cheapest, but a great 100 percent cotton shirt for the price. New! You can now save this product for later. This V-neck unfortunately made me feel like I was at an eighth-grade bowling party, uncomfortably pulling at my shirt so no one would notice how awkward I felt. The bottom quarter of the top clung to the waistband of my jeans, tugging the torso down in an unflattering manner, and the dimensions of the wide open V felt somehow at odds with the sleeves. If I looked too long in the mirror I’d see a big Mario M emerge where the V met the angles around my shoulders. It just wasn’t the shape I was looking for — Jungmaven’s hemp-and-cotton-blend fabric is lovely, and I think if I’d gone up one size it would have been a great oversize option for a different search. This test was an important reminder of why I believe length is the most make-or-break detail in a T-shirt (and why it’s such a personal preference, given how height and torso shape vary so vastly from one person to the next). New! You can now save this product for later. Well, “cheesecloth” is in the name, so I shouldn’t have been surprised to find that my bra was on full display underneath this Los Angeles Apparel tee. It’s supremely soft, but with a sheer composition and a V that plunges confidently into sternum territory, it’s not very wearable for the day-to-day. The gauzy fabric is a combination of cotton and elastane that suctions to the body with vigor, like the shirt comes pre-drenched in club sweat and a good time. The one is decidedly more “Party Rock Anthem” than CBK. New! You can now save this product for later. This J.Crew tee is a loose 100 percent cotton option that falls at the hip, and I went one size down for a fit that was relaxed but not oversize. What I like most about the tee is its wide, rounded V — it leads the eye slowly from the shoulder down the chest and meets into a curve right before the view gets risqué. But the material was thinner than most others I tried, and while it was a perfectly fine T-shirt paired with jeans, I wouldn’t be eager to wear it anywhere fancier than the grocery store. It’s a few rungs above a drugstore three-pack T-shirt but not particularly memorable. New! You can now save this product for later. The design details of this Madewell top are very similar to the Flore Flore option below. Just like Flore Flore, it features a high tight V, taut short sleeves, a just-above-the-hip length, and even has a similar center-back seam — only it retails for much cheaper. At first touch, it felt like it might be a promising dupe. The fabric is luxuriously thick with an impressive amount of stretch for its 100 percent cotton makeup. But when I put it on, the price difference felt immediately noticeable. The fit was just okay: The hem bunched a little awkwardly at my jeans, and at least on my own T-shirt, the V was wonky. It jeered toward the left side of my chest by a millimeter or so, and while I’m sure no one else would notice, it’s something I would think about every time I put it on. Following the advice of the reviews I went one size up, but I think my normal size would have been fine too. New! You can now save this product for later. The second-place T-shirts turned out to be the cheapest and priciest of the bunch, including this Uniqlo option. Though the shirt leans more casual, this V can go anywhere — deep enough to bare some clavicle but high enough to be appropriate for school pickup. It’s a tad longer than my preferred length, but it didn’t pucker uncomfortably over my jeans like some others. The hem rested gracefully over my belt loops with no torso-tugging in sight. I’m already a big fan of Uniqlo’s never-pretentious and always-efficient T-shirts, and I’m an even bigger fan of when the brand uses 100 percent cotton fabrics for its pieces, as with this one. A natural-fiber T-shirt at this price point that also looks good is like a needle in a polyester haystack. New! You can now save this product for later. I’ve been lusting after Flore Flore’s cotton basics for a while now, so I had the highest expectations for this one. It’s a really good shirt — made with a weighty 100 percent organic cotton featuring a gently rounded V — but it pinched a bit in the armpit area despite me going one size up. I think this is a model V-neck for so many others on the market, but as the most expensive piece in the lot, I needed it to fit perfectly to be the winner. I also ended up trying on its sleeveless sister in my pursuit, the Jill Tank in my regular size, and was shocked at how much I preferred it over the T-shirt. The T-shirt dropped me in V-neck limbo — the tank lifted me up to V-neck heaven. It wasn’t what I was looking for, but it gave me a new V-shaped rabbit hole to climb down. New! You can now save this product for later. This is Leset’s V-neck version of its cult-favorite Margo tee. It’s got a boxier relaxed fit, a 100 percent cotton makeup, and one of the lowest V’s of the bunch. It might even show off a flash of cleavage in the right push-up bra (I don’t own one, otherwise I would’ve thrown it on in the name of journalistic research). I went one size up from my usual and couldn’t have loved the fit more. It has a true short sleeve (not a cap or a drooping arm tube) and hits at my ideal length, showing a sliver of midriff when paired with low-rise pants and offering perfect modesty against mid- to high-rises. The fabric is so dreamy — by far the softest of the lot — and it’s got me fantasizing about replacing all my ratty pajama T-shirts with Margos in every color and silhouette. Of course, if I had a drawer full of Margos, I’d never dare delegate such coveted tees to a life of house arrest. Guess I need doubles of them all. New! You can now save this product for later. This Kotn number is the closest I got to the curved V, form-fitting, hip-hugging cotton T-shirt I was looking for. The length feels just right, there’s no pinching in the armpits, and it’s made with a medium-weight 100 percent Egyptian cotton that’s not too thick for a sticky summer day. With the proper swap of bottoms, this tee is as well-suited for a Michelin-starred dinner as it is for hot yoga with Christy. The V is high, slightly rounded, and not too in-your-face — an approachable starter V for those who remain only V-curious. It too feels very similar to the Flore Flore and Madewell tees, but I much prefer the fit of this one, and it’s priced low enough to justify owning one in every color. title: Edwin “Ed” V. Schepers, 74, St. Anthony - Dubois County Free Press, Inc.
content:
Edwin “Ed” V. Schepers, 74, of St. Anthony, passed away surrounded by family at 10:30 a.m. on Saturday, June 13, 2026, at Norton Hospital in Louisville, Kentucky. Ed was born in Jasper on November 19, 1951, to Frank and Hilda (Merkley) Schepers. He married Trina Messmer on April 22, 1972, at St. Anthony Catholic Church in St. Anthony, Indiana. He retired from Southern Indiana Hardwoods, where he had worked for over 30 years. He was a member of Divine Mercy Parish – St. Anthony Catholic Church, the Celestine Community Club, the Schellville Conservation Club, the St. Anthony Conservation Club, and the Birdseye Conservation Club. Ed enjoyed playing horseshoes, playing cards, especially Sheepshead, mushroom hunting, watching NASCAR, and spending time with family and friends. He was also very well known for handing out suckers to any children that he met. He is survived by his wife of 54 years, Trina Schepers of St. Anthony; four children, Bonnie (Brent) Lane of Birdseye, Greg (Angie) Schepers of North Port, Fla., Terry Schepers of Ferdinand, and Jonathon (Brittany) Schepers of Birdseye; nine grandchildren, Lexie and Colin Lane, Bryce, Desiree, and Grant Schepers, Ruby and Harmony Schepers, and Carter and Loren Schepers; siblings, Norma Mitchell, Clara (Mike) Blount, Allan Schepers, Susie (Richard) Dooley, Dorothy Persohn, Sandy Deich, Barbara Strange,  and Janet Schepers; one sister-in-law, Eileen Schepers; and many nieces and nephews. Preceding him in death are three brothers, Leroy, Jim, and Tom Schepers, four brothers-in-law, Emmett Mitchell, Mike Persohn, Roger Deich, and Randy Strange. A Mass of Christian Burial for Edwin Schepers will be held at 11:00 a.m. on Wednesday, June 17, 2026, at St. Anthony Catholic Church in St. Anthony, Indiana, with burial to follow in the church cemetery. A visitation will be held from 9:00 a.m. until the 11:00 a.m. service time at the church on Wednesday. Memorial contributions may be made to Divine Mercy Parish or to the wishes of the family. Online condolences may be made at www.becherkluesner.com.

title: Hyundai Ioniq V fastback revealed 66.8 kWh battery and 620 km range - CarNewsChina.com
content: The Hyundai Ioniq V electric fastback from the Beijing Hyundai joint venture revealed a 66.8 kWh LFP battery for 620 km of CLTC range. This 4.9-meter model will enter the Chinese market in 2026 with a 27-inch screen and an electric motor for 168 kW (225 hp). The Hyundai Ioniq V made its official debut at the Beijing Auto Show 2026 as the Korean automaker aims to win back China. According to China EV DataTracker, Hyundai delivered 6,500 units in the Middle Kingdom in May, down 8.9% Year-Over-Year. The Ioniq V was previously seen in China in the wild. According to the latest tax reduction list shared by the Chinese Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the entry-level Ioniq V adopts a 53.5 kWh LFP pack from CATL that powers a 140 kW (188 hp) electric motor. This fastback boasts an electric range of 520 – 540 km under CLTC conditions, depending on the equipment. It is worth noting that the battery weighs 395 kg. The entry-level Ioniq V’s curb weight lies between 1,707 and 1,737 kg. The long-range variant of the Hyundai Ioniq V has a 66.8 kWh LFP battery manufactured by CATL. It is paired with a 168 kW (225 hp). The car’s range reaches 620 – 650 km under CLTC conditions. The battery pack weighs 465 kg. And the long-range model has a curb weight of 1,782 – 1,808 kg. The Hyundai Ioniq V will also be available with an EREV powertrain in the future. The Hyundai Ioniq V boasts hefty dimensions of 4900/1890/1470 mm and a wheelbase of 2,900 mm. It adopts a sleek styling with a bonnet forming a single line with the windshield. Other features include semi-hidden door handles and split headlamps. The car’s interior adopts a large 27-inch dual-screen setup. Other highlights include a Momenta-developed assisted driving system and an 800V high-voltage system.
